doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Tape splicing with razor blades
summary: Rowe and Parker share amazement at tape editing, including a tape op who cut a square out of 24-track tape on a Phoebe Snow record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I had a moment in the studio once, I wonder if you had a moment like this. The first time I saw tape sliced with a razor blade and hooked back together I said what is that? This actually works?

Yeah. No it was amazing. There’s some great tape operators and engineers who were amazing with a razor blade and it’s a crucial, very scary moment when you see the razor blade cut the 24-track tape or 16-track tape back in the days, and then put it back together. And oh my God, it sounds okay. I even saw a guy who was working with Phil Ramone on a production at A&R slice just a square out of a 24-track tape. So not just a
razor blade but like an Exacto knife — like a little quarter inch square of tape and then replace that. Somebody hit a microphone or something and there was no other way to repair it than that.
He sliced — he put a piece back in?

Into the 24-track tape — I think it was on a Phoebe Snow record and I can’t remember the tape op’s name. He said, “No I’ll do this, I’ll do this, I’ll fix it.” And he had an Exacto knife you know and a little quarter inch square, sliced that out of the — to locate it for one thing it was amazing. But it worked you know. He got rid of the unwanted noise.
